records.title: Chiral Polyhedra in 3-Dimensional Geometries and from a Petrie-Coxeter Construction (paper A, PETCOX) — cites (B)
records.authors: Javier Bracho, Isabel Hubard, Daniel Pellicer
records.how_found: Listed as citing (B) in OpenAlex (W3197857784), Semantic Scholar (arXiv record of B), zbMATH (rf:6394874) and Google Scholar cluster 18013071674759774703; author-copy PDF fetched and text-extracted with PyPDF2
records.theorem_or_page: Section 4, subsections 'Chiral polyhedra from {4,3,3} and {3,3,4}', 'from {5,3,3} and {3,3,5}', 'from the starry regular polytopes', and the 'Summary of chiral polyhedra from the regular polytopes' table (author copy pp. 23-28)
records.verbatim_quote: "The general H_α({4,3,3}) has type {8_{1,3},3}. In this case, for α = 0 no vertices come together, so we still have a chiral polyhedron H_0({4,3,3}), which was taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope in S^3 (or R^4) in [3]." ... "The type of H_α({5,3,3}) is {30_{1,11},3}, and for α = 0 no vertices identify, so that H_0({5,3,3}) can be taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope, but not H_1({5,3,3}) in which four vertices come together." ... "For {3,3,5/2} the type of H_α is {30_{7,13},3}. Vertices that collapse at α = 0,1 are 4,1 respectivelly. The group G is of order 1440." ... "For {5,3,5/2} the type of H_α is {12_{1,5},3}; it remains a polyhedron at α = 0,1. The group G is of order 144." Summary table (Polytope T / Type of H_α(T) / #(G) / [G:Γ+] / collapses at α=(0,1)): {3,3,3} {5_{1,2},3} 60 1 (4,4); {4,3,3} {8_{1,3},3} 48 4 (1,2); {3,4,3} {12_{1,5},4} 192 3 (2,2); {5,3,3} {30_{1,11},3} 1440 5 (1,4); {3,5,5/2} {20_{1,9},5} 1200 6 (2,2); {5,5/2,5} {15_{1,4},5/2} 7200 1 (12,12); {5,3,5/2} {12_{1,5},3} 144 50 (1,1); {3,3,5/2} {30_{7,13},3} 1440 5 (4,1); {3,5/2,5} {20_{3,7},5/2} 1200 6 (2,2); {5/2,5,5/2} {15_{2,7},5} 7200 1 (12,12). "The regular polyhedra P_T arising from the polytopes T={4,3,3}, T={3,4,3} and T={5,3,5/2} can be found in Michael Hartley's Atlas ... they correspond to the polytopes {8,3}*96, {12,4}*384e and {12,3}*288"; "the regular polyhedra arising from T={5,3,3} and T={3,3,5/2} are isomorphic of type {30,3} and are listed as R97.9. The polyhedra from the polytopes T={3,5,5/2} and T={3,5/2,5} are of type {20,5} and also isomorphic, listed as R151.11." "when T={3,3,3} ... H_α(T) is a chiral realisation of the dodecahedron in E^4."
records.relevance: The only citing work that states which PETCOX polyhedra can be facets of chiral 4-polytopes. It asserts (without construction) that H_0({5,3,3}) 'can be taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope'; it records that H_1({3,3,5/2}) (= the candidate H_0({5/2,3,3}), type {30_{7,13},3}, group order 1440) has no vertex collapse at α=1, and that both H_0 and H_1 of {5,3,5/2} remain polyhedra (the facets used in (C)). It constructs no new 4-polytope. It also identifies the abstract facets as the maps {8,3}*96, {12,4}*384e, {12,3}*288, R97.9, R151.11 and the dodecahedron.

records.title: Open problems on k-orbit polytopes — cites (B)
records.how_found: OpenAlex cites:W1970228947; Semantic Scholar; zbMATH rf:6394874; Google Scholar cluster
records.verbatim_quote: "Regular polytopes of full rank were classified in [46, Theorem 11.2], where it is also stated that there are no chiral polytopes of full rank. This claim turned out to be false; there are both finite chiral 4-polytopes in E^4 [5] and infinite 4-polytopes in E^3 [66]. It is natural now to ask for the classification of full rank chiral polytopes. Problem 20. Describe all chiral polytopes of full rank." Also Problem 23: "Describe all two-orbit polytopes of full rank."
records.relevance: Poses the classification of full-rank chiral polytopes as an open problem (2016/2018); mentions no further finite chiral 4-polytope in E^4 beyond Roli's cube and no statement on facets of full-rank chiral 4-polytopes.

records.title: A chiral 4-polytope in R^3 — cites (B)
records.how_found: OpenAlex; Google Scholar cluster (also listed a duplicate copy at repositorioccm.matmor.unam.mx/handle/123456789/163)
records.verbatim_quote: "In this paper we describe an infinite chiral 4-polytope in the Euclidean 3-space. This builds on previous work of Bracho, Hubard and the author, where a finite chiral 4-polytope in the Euclidean 4-space is constructed. These two polytopes show that there are finite and infinite chiral polytopes of full rank as defined by McMullen."
records.relevance: Infinite full-rank chiral 4-polytope in E^3; no new finite chiral 4-polytope in E^4.

records.title: Quasi-Regular Polytopes of Full Rank — cites (B)
records.doi_or_url: 10.1007/s00454-021-00304-5 (abstract page fetched via link.springer.com after idp redirect)
records.how_found: OpenAlex; Semantic Scholar; zbMATH; Google Scholar cluster
records.theorem_or_page: Abstract; reference list (full text paywalled, not retrieved)
records.verbatim_quote: "A polytope P in some euclidean space is called quasi-regular if each facet F of P is regular and the symmetry group G(F) of F is a subgroup of the symmetry group G(P) of P." The page summary: the paper classifies quasi-regular polytopes of full rank that are not regular, plus discrete quasi-regular apeirotopes; "certain families are present in R^d if d is even, but are absent if d is odd." References include Bracho-Hubard-Pellicer (2014) "A finite chiral 4-polytope in R^4", Pellicer (2017a) "A chiral 4-polytope in R^3", Pellicer (2017b) "Chiral 4-polytopes in ordinary space".
records.relevance: Cites Roli's cube in the context of full-rank (quasi-)regular polytopes; no accessible statement constructing further chiral 4-polytopes in E^4.

records.title: On Roli's cube — cites (B)
records.venue: The Art of Discrete and Applied Mathematics; arXiv:2102.08796 (submitted 17 Feb 2021)
records.verbatim_quote: "First described in 2014, Roli's cube R is a chiral 4-polytope, faithfully realized in Euclidean 4-space (a situation earlier thought to be impossible). Here we describe R in a new way, determine its minimal regular cover, and reveal connections to the Möbius-Kantor configuration." ... "Chiral polytopes with realizations of 'full rank' had (incorrectly) been shown not to exist by Peter McMullen in [11, Theorem 11.2]. Mind you, these objects do seem to be elusive. Pellicer has proved in [15] that chiral polytopes of full rank can exist only in ranks 4 or 5." ... "Theorem 6.1. (a) The 4-polytope R is abstractly chiral of type {8,3,3}." ... "(b) The corresponding regular 4-polytope T has type {8,3,3} and is faithfully realized in E^8".
records.relevance: Re-describes Roli's cube via Petrie polygons of the 4-cube and its minimal regular cover; explicitly notes full-rank chiral polytopes 'seem to be elusive'; constructs no further chiral 4-polytope in E^4.

records.theorem_or_page: Section 'Contribución de la investigación' (pp. 3-4); 'Formación de recursos humanos' (p. 12)
records.verbatim_quote: "clasificar los poliedros esqueléticos quirales cuyo 1-esqueleto está contenido en la gráfica de un 4-politopo convexo regular. La estudiante Trejo, con apoyo de la Dra. Hubard, logró dar dicha clasificación, obteniendo únicamente 4 ejemplos." ... "una de las metas del proyecto fue la de usar los poliedros esqueléticos quirales cuyo 1-esqueleto está contenido en la gráfica de un 4-politopo convexo regular para construir 4-politopos quirales en el espacio euclidiano de 4 dimensiones. Este trabajo tuvo buenos resultados: de los 4 poliedros quirales que existen cuyo 1-esqueleto está contenido en la gráfica de un 4-politopo convexo regular, se determinaron cuáles de ellos se pueden extender." ... "el estudiante González Casanova trabajó con la Dra. Hubard y el Dr. Bracho en construir un par de nuevos 4-politpos quirales en el espacio de 4 dimensiones. Para esto, estudió a profundidad algunos 4-politopos estrellados regulares de dicho espacio y les aplicó una serie de operaciones para obtener poliedros quirales. Después, logró encontrar isometrías que lo han ayudado a extender los poliedros a 4-politopos quirales." Thesis record: "Nombre DANIEL GONZALEZ CASANOVA AZUELA Título de la tesis Dos 4-politops quirales de rango Director de la tesis JAVIER BRACHO CARPIZO Nivel Maestría" (title truncated in the PDF). Talk listed: "A family of chiral polyhedra with helical faces in R4 ... 10th Slovenian Conference on Graph Theory" (Trejo).
records.relevance: Independent confirmation that (i) exactly 4 chiral skeletal polyhedra have 1-skeleton in the graph of a convex regular 4-polytope (Trejo-Hubard) and that it was determined which of them extend to chiral 4-polytopes in E^4 (paper to be submitted), and (ii) the two new full-rank chiral 4-polytopes of (C) come from starry regular 4-polytopes; the thesis is directed by Bracho, master's level.

Key substantive findings for the research question: (1) No citing work constructs or names any finite chiral 4-polytope of full rank in E^4 other than Roli's cube; Monson (2021) remarks these objects 'do seem to be elusive'. (2) The only statements about PETCOX polyhedra as facets are in PETCOX itself: H_0({4,3,3}) 'was taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope in S^3 (or R^4) in [3]' and 'H_0({5,3,3}) can be taken as facet of a chiral 4-polytope, but not H_1({5,3,3})'; the summary table gives, for each of the 10 regular 4-polytopes, the type, group order, index [G:Γ+] and the number of vertices collapsing at α=0 and α=1 (e.g. {3,3,5/2}: (4,1), so H_1({3,3,5/2}) = the candidate H_0({5/2,3,3}) of type {30_{7,13},3} does not collapse; {5,3,5/2}: (1,1), the facets used in (C)). Note that PETCOX's phrasing for H_0({5,3,3}) is 'can be taken as facet' — no 4-polytope is constructed there, and no citing work has since constructed one. (3) Two unpublished works are documented: Bracho-González-Casanova-Hubard, 'Two new chiral 4-polytopes of full rank' ('In preparation' as of April 2026, ref. [1] of arXiv:2604.00185; the PAPIIT IN109023 report confirms they arise from starry regular 4-polytopes, thesis 'Dos 4-politop[o]s quirales de rango [completo]', director J. Bracho, master's level), and Hubard-Trejo, 'A family of skeletal chiral 3- and 4-polytopes in R^4' (ref. [31], 'Preprint'; the PAPIIT report states Trejo classified the chiral skeletal polyhedra whose 1-skeleton lies in the graph of a convex regular 4-polytope — 'únicamente 4 ejemplos' — and determined which of them extend to chiral 4-polytopes in E^4; a talk 'A family of chiral polyhedra with helical faces in R4' is listed). Neither preprint was found on arXiv or elsewhere. (4) Cunningham-Pellicer Problem 20 ('Describe all chiral polytopes of full rank') and Problem 23 remain the standing open problems in the citing literature; Pellicer 2021 restricts full-rank chiral polytopes to ranks 4 and 5.
